title: Beyond Outcome Gaps: Process-Aware Fairness Diagnosis for LLM-based Multi-Agent Decision Systems

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual substitution of gender-implied names in candidate resumes, tracking multi-agent hiring decisions, scores, and intermediate reasoning steps.
Manipulating implied age via experience year shifts in candidate resumes and evaluating the impact on intermediate and final hiring decisions.

Substituting country-specific identity-group names (e.g., majority/minority identities across 12 national contexts) in resumes and evaluating differences in multi-agent scrutiny, scoring, and hiring rates.
Injecting class-stratified, culturally specific hobbies and activities into resumes to evaluate differential treatment and reasoning in the agent evaluation process.
Varying university and city prestige tiers in candidate resumes to measure their impact on agent qualification judgments, intermediate scoring, and multi-agent deliberation.
Adding distinct career gap explanations (health, family care, layoff) to resumes and measuring the resulting agent suspicion and skeptical investigation requests.
